summary: Hitoshi Kato works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. In 1992, he held lecturer and research assistant posts, later becoming a professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017) and holding a post at Otani University.

Hitoshi Miyake is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1952–1956) and the University of Tokyo (~1956–1961), later serving as professor at Keio University (~1967–1999) and Kokugakuin University (~1999–2004).

Hitoshi Obara is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Hokkaido University, he served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart from approximately 1982 to 2015.
Hla Pe was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon, UCL, and SOAS University of London. He taught at SOAS beginning in 1948 and served there as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Yang earned a PhD at the University of Washington by 1994, studying under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Hogen Bays works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Having studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada, Bays serves as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.

Hojun Nagasaki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1962–1964) and held posts at Otani University (~1974–1999) and the Japanese Association for Jain Studies (1998).
Hokai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.

Hokei Idzumi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1905–1909) under Bunyiu Nanjio (~1905–1910) and served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1921 to 1947.
Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She was a doctoral candidate at Harvard University (~2000–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado around 2008.

Holmes Welch was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Francis Woodman Cleaves at Harvard University (~1946–1957) and later taught at Harvard (~1961–1976) and Yale University.

Hong Luo specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After completing a PhD at Peking University in 2007, Luo worked at the China Tibetology Research Center (2007–2017) and became a professor at Sichuan University in 2018.
Hongyue Guo works in sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo studied under Xubang Qi and earned a PhD at Indiana University under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp (attested 2007).

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held lecturer and professor posts at Minobusan Junior College, a professorship at Minobusan University (attested 1996), and served as director of the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh specializes in sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Toh studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu, earning a PhD from Harvard University by 2004.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Cambridge and earned a PhD at SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden, later serving as Field Director for the Greater-India Research Committee (~1934–1941) and Vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1947–1968).

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. He held posts with the East India Company, served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860), and was Director of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Horace L. Friess was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Columbia University and Heidelberg. He taught at Columbia from 1919, later becoming Buttenwieser Professor (1962–1966), and also held a post at Johns Hopkins.
Horkhang Sonam Palbar was a Tibetologist who studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang and Gendun Chophel (~1946–1951).

Horst Lasic is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995), completed his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999, and became a lecturer there in 1999.
